mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary regime, which increases discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when inflation exceeds 6% simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a rise in the housing market (HOUST up > 5% YoY) signals weakening consumer demand offset by housing strength, resulting in muted S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST YoY change > 5%
regime_hint: late-cycle consumption slowdown with housing resilience
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 70% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when labor market indicators (UNRATE) are rising.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 6% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered months, or the mechanism fails during periods of strong productivity growth (INDPRO rising > 1% MoM).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenue prospects and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered months, or the mechanism fails when commodity prices are rising sharply.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and core CPI above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual tightening in monetary and price pressures, which increases risk-off sentiment and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > previous 12-month avg AND CPIAUCSL > previous 12-month avg
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when labor market indicators are improving sharply.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid acceleration in payroll employment growth (PAYEMS monthly change > 0.5%) alongside a flat or declining unemployment rate signals a tight labor market, which compresses profit margins and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 0.5% AND UNRATE monthly change <= 0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of strong productivity growth.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) of more than 1% for four consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days regardless of other conditions.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of strong export growth (not measured here but implied by GDP).

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated monthly decline in both industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) of more than 1% signals a broad-based contraction in supply-side activity, which depresses earnings and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1.0% AND HOUST monthly change < -1.0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 45% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when monetary policy is strongly expansionary (FEDFUNDS < 1%).
